reader.requirement: At COBOL-85 every explicitly referenced nonunique user-defined name must be made unique by a sequence of qualifiers (format 1: group/record names, file-name or cd-name; format 2: section-name for a paragraph) that precludes ambiguity: the compiler must resolve a reference whose qualifiers (any sufficient subset, in successively more inclusive order) single out one item, and refuse one that still matches several, names a non-superior, or orders qualifiers wrongly; index-names take no qualifiers at 85.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.Check(Constructs.QualifiedIndexName2002): a qualified index-name is refused at 85 (index-names cannot be qualified, §1985:X.1.3.8.3)
Edition.Permissive only (warning + first declaration); no edition switch

reader.edition-search: Grepped NameResolution.cs, QualifiedNameClasses.cs, Model/SymbolTable.cs, Model/FileModel.cs, FileControlBinder.cs, Procedure/Verbs/KeyedIoBinder.cs for DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/CobolVersion/IsAvailable: only the QualifiedIndexName2002 gate (and an unrelated PADDING arm in FileControlBinder) consult the edition; data-name, condition-name, record-key and paragraph-name qualification is edition-blind.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes, for index-names only: 85 refuses IX OF table (COBOL0900), 2023 accepts it; data-name, condition-name, file/cd-name qualifiers and paragraph OF section resolve identically
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers an unqualified duplicated index-name only; the probes add data-name qualification by partial and full qualifier sets, condition-names, file-name and cd-name qualifiers, RECORD KEY and READ KEY qualification, subscripted qualified tables, paragraph OF section, and the refusal forms

probes.printed: --std 85 EXIT 0: G1 G2 G1 / G1-ON / G2-OFF / 47 / UNQ / ONE
probes.expected: X OF G1 (skipping SUB), X IN SUB OF G2, condition-names qualified by group and by conditional variable chain, EA OF TA (2)/EA IN TB (2) = 4,7, unneeded qualification legal (SRL2.2), RECORD KEY IS K OF R1 / K OF F2, MOVE ... TO D IN R2 IN F2, READ F1 KEY IS K OF R1 reads ONE

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL1639 'X OF SUB' does not uniquely identify a data item — 2 declarations of 'X' match
probes.expected: refused: qualifiers do not preclude ambiguity

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL1639 'X OF A' ... 2 declarations of 'X' match (A.X and A.B.X)
probes.expected: refused: X OF A matches two items

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL1639 'X OF G1 OF SUB' ... not under the given qualifiers
--std 85: COBOL1639 'X OF G3' ... not under the given qualifier (G3)
probes.expected: refused: qualifier is not a superior
X OF B OF A is unique -> BX

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL1639 RECORD KEY 'K' does not uniquely identify a data item — 2 declarations match
--std 85: COBOL2121 PERFORM 'PX': the reference is not unique (PX in S1 and S2, referenced from S0)
probes.expected: refused; c5pq.cob with PX OF S1 / PX IN S2 prints S1-PX / S2-PX

probes.printed: --std 85 EXIT 0: ABC         |XY  | (QN OF CDIN, QN IN CDOUT-REC, QN OF CDOUT); c5cdu.cob unqualified QN: COBOL1639
probes.expected: cd-name is a format 1 qualifier at 85; unqualified nonunique QN refused

probes.printed: --std 85: COBOL0900 a qualified index-name requires COBOL-2002 (x3); --std 2023 prints 05

reader.notes: Qualified references resolve when the qualifier set singles out one item (any sufficient subset, file-name and cd-name qualifiers included) and every ambiguous, misordered or non-superior qualification is refused with COBOL1639/COBOL2121, at 85 as at 2023. The only edition arm, the 2002 qualified-index-name gate, refuses IX OF table at 85 as §1985:X.1.3.8.3 requires.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: r5a level-66 RN declared in two records, RENAMES operands qualified (F1 OF R2 THRU F2 OF R2), RN OF R1 / RN IN R2 / A OF A (an elementary A inside 01 A) print ABCD / EFGH / AA; the first form with unqualified RENAMES F1 THRU F2 (F1 also in R2) is refused COBOL1639, as SRL2.1 and §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5 allow; r5b SD file-name as qualifier (K OF SF, V OF SF), V OF G OF SREC, V OF G OF W1, V IN W2 skipping a level, K OF W1 print SK / SV / WV / W2 / W1; r5c V OF G where G is itself nonunique is refused COBOL1639. Checks: 'OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.4 ... the text is in SRL2.4'; 'OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR3 ... the text is in SR3'.
